title: Review of provisions related to International Securities Identification Number (ISIN) for debt securities issued on private placement basis
text:
CIRCULAR

HO/17/11/24(8)2026-DDHS-POD1/I/23125/2026 October 07, 2026

To,
Issuers of listed debt securities;
All Stock Exchanges;
All Depositories

Sub: Review of provisions related to International Securities Identification Number (ISIN) for debt securities issued on private placement basis
1. Chapter VIII of SEBI Master Circular for Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities, Securitised Debt Instruments, Security Receipts, Municipal Debt Securities and Commercial Paper dated October 15, 2025 (“NCS Master Circular”) deals with specifications related to ISIN for debt securities.
2. Based on the feedback received from market participants, in order to enhance ease of fund raising and Asset Liability Management by issuers, it has been decided to increase the maximum number of ISINs maturing in a financial year for debt securities issued on private placement basis.

title: Review of provisions related to International Securities Identification Number (ISIN) for debt securities issued on private placement basis
text:
it has been decided to increase the maximum number of ISINs maturing in a financial year for debt securities issued on private placement basis.
3. Accordingly, para 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 of the NCS Master Circular shall be replaced with the following:

“1.1 A maximum number of seventeen ISINs maturing in any financial year shall be allowed for an issuer of debt securities. In addition, a further six ISINs shall also be available for the issuance of the capital gains tax debt securities by the authorized issuers under section 54EC of the Income Tax Act, 1961 on private placement basis.

title: Review of provisions related to International Securities Identification Number (ISIN) for debt securities issued on private placement basis
text:
of the capital gains tax debt securities by the authorized issuers under section 54EC of the Income Tax Act, 1961 on private placement basis.
1.2 Out of the seventeen ISINs maturing in a financial year, the bifurcation of ISINs shall be as under: a. A maximum of twelve ISINs maturing per financial year shall be allowed for plain vanilla debt securities. Within this limit of twelve ISINs, the issuer can issue both secured and unsecured debt securities. b. In case the total outstanding amount across the twelve ISINs, maturing in a given financial year, reaches Rs. 15,000 Crore, then for each additional issuance of Rs. 3000 Crore, one additional ISIN may be permitted to mature in the same financial year. A maximum of five ISINs maturing per financial year shall be allowed for structured debt securities, market linked debt securities, Floating Rate Bonds (FRBs), Zero Coupon Bonds (ZCBs) and Debt Capital instruments (Tier II bonds). Any existing ISINs pertaining to Floating Rate Bonds (FRBs), Zero Coupon Bonds (ZCBs) and Debt Capital instruments (Tier II bonds) issued prior to the date of this circular, which are outstanding and scheduled to mature in any subsequent financial year, shall be grandfathered to avoid any unintended breach of ISIN cap.

However, if the aggregate number of such outstanding legacy ISINs maturing in any subsequent financial year already equals or exceeds five, the issuer shall not issue any further new ISIN(s) under this sub- clause (including for structured debt securities, market linked debt securities, FRBs, ZCBs and Debt Capital instruments/ Tier II bonds) for that specific financial year, until the total number of maturing ISINs in the said category falls below five.
1.3 Where an issuer issues only structured/ market linked debt securities/ FRBs/ ZCBs/ Debt Capital instruments (Tier II bonds), the maximum number of ISINs allowed to mature in a financial year shall be twelve.”

4.1. Government of India (GoI) serviced/ Extra Budgetary Resources (EBR) bonds
4.2. Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) Debt Securities, issued in terms of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021
5. All other provisions of Chapter VIII (Specifications related to ISIN for debt securities) of the NCS Master Circular shall remain unchanged.

title: Exemption from the requirement of mandatory merchant banker appointment for debt issued through private placement by certain listed issuers
text:
CIRCULAR

HO/17/11/24(7)2026-DDHS-POD1/ I/23122/2026 October 07, 2026

To,
Issuers of listed debt securities;
All Stock Exchanges;
All Depositories
All SEBI-Registered Merchant Bankers

Sub: Exemption from the requirement of mandatory merchant banker appointment for debt issued through private placement by certain listed issuers

title: Exemption from the requirement of mandatory merchant banker appointment for debt issued through private placement by certain listed issuers
text:
Exemption from the requirement of mandatory merchant banker appointment for debt issued through private placement by certain listed issuers
1. Clause 1.3 of Chapter V of SEBI Master Circular for issue and listing of Non-Convertible Securities, Securitised Debt Instruments, Security Receipts, Municipal Debt Securities and Commercial Paper dated October 15, 2025 (“NCS Master Circular”), inter-alia, states the following: “1.3. The Issuer may issue debt security or non-convertible redeemable preference share on private placement basis at a face value of Rs. Ten Thousand,

i) Subject to the following conditions: a) The issuer shall appoint at least one Merchant Banker. Provided that the role, responsibilities and obligations of the Merchant Banker(s) shall be same as they would be in case of public issue of debt security or non-convertible redeemable preference share.

title: Exemption from the requirement of mandatory merchant banker appointment for debt issued through private placement by certain listed issuers
text:
of the Merchant Banker(s) shall be same as they would be in case of public issue of debt security or non-convertible redeemable preference share.
b) Such debt security or non-convertible redeemable preference share shall be interest/ dividend bearing security paying coupon/ dividend at regular intervals with a fixed maturity without any structured obligations……”
2. Based on the feedback received from market participants, in order to enhance ease of issuing debt securities and to expand access of high-rated securities to retail investors, it has been decided to relax the requirement of merchant banker appointment, subject to certain conditions specified in the subsequent paras.

title: Exemption from the requirement of mandatory merchant banker appointment for debt issued through private placement by certain listed issuers
text:
it has been decided to relax the requirement of merchant banker appointment, subject to certain conditions specified in the subsequent paras.
3. Accordingly, para 1.3 of the NCS Master Circular shall be replaced as under: “1.3. The Issuer may issue debt security or non-convertible redeemable preference share on private placement basis at a face value of Rs. Ten Thousand, subject to the following conditions: a) The issuer shall appoint at least one Merchant Banker, and the role, responsibilities and obligations of the Merchant Banker(s) shall be same as they would be in case of public issue of debt security or non-convertible redeemable preference share. b) The Issuer may not appoint a Merchant Banker, subject to fulfilment of all the following conditions: i. The Issuer is registered/ regulated by a financial sector regulator in India, viz. SEBI, RBI, IRDAI or PFRDA. ii.

title: Exemption from the requirement of mandatory merchant banker appointment for debt issued through private placement by certain listed issuers
text:
i. The Issuer is registered/ regulated by a financial sector regulator in India, viz. SEBI, RBI, IRDAI or PFRDA. ii.
The Issuer is listed in any segment on any of the recognized Stock Exchange(s) for a period of at least one year and there are no pending fines or penalties levied by SEBI/ Stock Exchanges for non-compliance with any of the applicable provisions of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in respect of the issuer. Stock Exchange(s) shall confirm the above at the time of granting in-principle approval for the issue. iii. The Issuer has not defaulted in the last three financial years and the current financial year in respect of the redemption/ repayment or interest/ dividend payable in respect of its debt securities, non-convertible redeemable preference shares, securitised debt instruments, commercial papers, deposits or loans. The Issuer shall submit a certificate from the Statutory Auditor to this effect to the Stock Exchange. iv.

title: Exemption from the requirement of mandatory merchant banker appointment for debt issued through private placement by certain listed issuers
text:
The Issuer shall submit a certificate from the Statutory Auditor to this effect to the Stock Exchange. iv.
The debt security issued shall be unsubordinated/ senior and “secured” by a first or pari passu charge on the identifiable assets of the issuer. However, in case of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs)/ Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and Statutory Bodies, the debt security may be secured or unsecured. v. The debt security shall be rated at least AA- or above on the date of private placement. In case of multiple ratings, the lowest rating shall be considered for determining eligibility for exemption.”
4. Stock exchange(s) shall specify suitable operational requirements such as disclosure formats/ submissions required to be made by the issuer to comply with the conditions specified above.
5. All other provisions of Chapter V of the NCS Master Circular shall remain unchanged.

Applicability: The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all listed and proposed to be listed issuances of Non-Convertible Securities (NCS), Commercial Papers (CPs), Securitised Debt Instruments (SDIs), Security Receipts (SRs), and Structured Debt / Market Linked Debentures (MLDs), whether issued by way of public issue or private placement.

2.1.2. Abridged Prospectus
2.1.3. Private Placement Memorandum

2.10. Wherever CRA mentions “Issuer is Not Cooperating” (“INC”), the credit risk- o-meter shall be displayed in following manner in such cases, with arrow directed towards the INC. The INC status shall also be reflected in the textual disclosure below the credit risk-o-meter.
2.11. Disclaimers:

text:
The INC status shall also be reflected in the textual disclosure below the credit risk-o-meter.
2.11. Disclaimers:
2.11.1. Issuers/OBPPs shall incorporate the following disclaimer in Offer document, Abridged Prospectus and Private Placement Memorandum below the credit risk-o-meter, and display the same suitably on their web and mobile platform:

“The Credit risk-o-meter is based on evaluation of the credit risk of the issuer and does not constitute investment advice or a recommendation to invest. Investments in debt securities are also subject to market and liquidity risks.”

title: Introduction of Credit Risk-o-Meter as an additional disclosure mechanism for debt securities
text:
Investments in debt securities are also subject to market and liquidity risks.”
2.11.2. In case of unsecured perpetual bonds (such as AT1 bonds), the Issuers/OBPPs shall incorporate the following disclaimer in Offer document, Abridged Prospectus and Private Placement Memorandum below the credit risk-o-meter, and display the same suitably on their web and mobile platform:

“The Credit Risk-o-Meter is based on evaluation of the credit risk of the issuer and does not reflect the unique structural risks associated with Unsecured Perpetual Bonds (such as AT1 Bonds). These instruments may carry the risk of total loss of invested capital. Investors are advised to read the Information Memorandum/Private placement Memorandum carefully before investing."
2.12. Additional requirements for OBPPs:

title: Introduction of Credit Risk-o-Meter as an additional disclosure mechanism for debt securities
text:
Additional requirements for OBPPs:
2.12.1. Any change in credit risk-o-meter of the debt security shall be communicated by OBPP on their platform, within 24 hours of receiving intimation of rating change from NSDL/CDSL.
2.12.2. OBPPs shall display the Credit risk-o-meter on the Bond Listing & Bond details page where all other details are prominently displayed before investment action buttons.
2.12.3. OBPPs shall ensure that the credit risk-o-meter is displayed or printed in all forms of advertisements that explicitly reference the rating of the debt security, irrespective of the medium or format of such advertisements.
2.12.4. In case of advertisements published in monochrome format, a QR code shall be provided along with credit risk-o-meter to enable investors to access the website of OBPP/Issuer and view the Credit Risk-o-Meter in the prescribed colour-coded format.

Dear Sir/ Madam,

Subject: Review of certain aspects of the Closing Auction Session, market timings and settlement methodology for derivatives contracts
1. SEBI vide circular dated January 16, 2026, had introduced the Closing Auction Session (CAS) in the equity cash segment of Stock Exchanges with the objective, inter alia, of facilitating transparent and efficient price discovery of the closing price of securities. The said circular also specified the framework for determination of settlement prices of stock and index derivative contracts by the Clearing Corporations, on the expiry day, based on the closing prices determined under the CAS framework.

2. Subsequent to the implementation of the CAS framework, SEBI undertook a review of certain aspects relating to the functioning of CAS, market timings and the methodology for determination of settlement prices of derivative contracts. In this regard, a Consultation Paper dated September 12, 2026, was issued seeking public comments on the aforesaid aspects. The review was undertaken with a view to ensuring efficient price discovery and orderly functioning of the cash and derivatives segments.

title: Margin Waiver on Subsequent Buy/Sell Transactions Post Early Pay-In (EPI) in Cash Segment
text:
HO/(320)2026-MRD-POD2/I/24141/2026 October 22, 2026
To,
All Recognised Stock Exchanges
All Recognised Clearing Corporations (CCs)
All Depositories
All Stock Brokers
Sir/Madam,

Subject: Margin Waiver on Subsequent Buy/Sell Transactions Post Early Pay-In (EPI) in Cash Segment
1. Exchanges/Clearing Corporations (CCs) in consultation with SEBI, have issued various circulars/ guidelines on Margin collection and Reporting for the cases where the client has completed Early Pay-in of securities.

title: Margin Waiver on Subsequent Buy/Sell Transactions Post Early Pay-In (EPI) in Cash Segment
text:
issued various circulars/ guidelines on Margin collection and Reporting for the cases where the client has completed Early Pay-in of securities.
2. The said circulars/ guidelines inter-alia stipulate that in respect of sale of shares by a client for which EPI request via Block mechanism has been accepted, the same may be considered as margin collected towards peak margin for the said sale transaction. Further, in respect of sale of shares by a client for which EPI request via Block mechanism has been accepted and credit entry is posted of the sale value of the shares in the ledger account of the client, EPI value may be considered as margin collected towards subsequent margin requirement of the client. The sale value up to 100% of such securities (EPI value) shall be available as Margin for other positions across all the segments.

title: Margin Waiver on Subsequent Buy/Sell Transactions Post Early Pay-In (EPI) in Cash Segment
text:
The sale value up to 100% of such securities (EPI value) shall be available as Margin for other positions across all the segments.
3. In this context, taking into account the proposals received from the Broker ISF, recommendations of Risk Management Review Committee (RMRC) of SEBI and internal deliberations, it is decided that where a client has a net sell obligation in a settlement; and the EPI request for the sold securities has been successfully accepted by the CC, the CC shall, on a real-time basis, not collect margin from the Trading Member (TM)/ Clearing Member (CM) on the subsequent buy/sell positions of the client, up to the amount of such accepted EPI.
4. The aforesaid facility shall be implemented in the following manner:
4.1. Upon EPI accepted, CC on trade date shall compute the available value of EPI which shall be lower of the value of EPI done or value of securities sold.

title: Margin Waiver on Subsequent Buy/Sell Transactions Post Early Pay-In (EPI) in Cash Segment
text:
EPI accepted, CC on trade date shall compute the available value of EPI which shall be lower of the value of EPI done or value of securities sold.
4.2. Upon the client taking position basis the EPI on same trade date in cash segment, CC shall check the availability of client margin after reducing the available value of EPI.
4.3. If client squares off the sale position in securities for which client has availed EPI benefit, the value of EPI shall be removed and any shortfall in margins at client level due to such removal of EPI value, shall be blocked from the proprietary collateral of TM/CM by the CC. This condition will not be applicable to Trade for trade (TFT) securities as such transactions are settled on gross basis.

Madam/ Sir,

Sub: Review of regulatory requirement for maintenance of call records of institutional clients by Research Analysts or Research Entities
1. Regulation 25(1)(vii) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Research Analysts) Regulations, 2014 (RA Regulations), inter-alia, mandates a Research Analyst/ Research Entity (RA/ RE) to maintain records of communication, including call recordings.
2. The SEBI Master Circular for Research Analysts dated February 6, 20261 (Master Circular for RAs), provides a consolidation of the directions/ instructions applicable on RAs/ REs. In particular, paragraph 1.13 of Chapter 1 and paragraph 33 of

title: Review of regulatory requirement for maintenance of call records of institutional clients by Research Analysts or Research Entities
text:
In particular, paragraph 1.13 of Chapter 1 and paragraph 33 of
Annexure I of Chapter VII of the Master Circular for RAs, inter alia, specify the requirements pertaining to maintenance of records, including call recordings by RAs/ REs.
3. Based on the representations received from the market participants and as a part of SEBI’s ongoing efforts to enhance the ease of doing business, amendment to Regulation 25(1)(vii) of the RA Regulations have been notified, thereby relaxing the requirement upon RAs/ REs to maintain call recordings of communications with clients which are institutional investors.
1 Circular ref. no. HO/38/12/11(1)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4360/2026;

title: Review of regulatory requirement for maintenance of call records of institutional clients by Research Analysts or Research Entities
text:
4. Accordingly, it has been decided to suitably modify and replace the relevant provisions of the Master Circular for RAs, as under:
4.1. Paragraph 1.13 of Chapter I of Master Circular for RAs, shall be replaced with the following:

“1.13. KYC requirements and maintenance of record

a. As provided under Regulation 25(1) of RA Regulations, RA or research entity shall follow the KYC procedure for their fee paying clients and maintain KYC records for their clients as specified by SEBI from time to time.

b. Regulation 25 (1) of RA Regulations also provides that RA or research entity shall maintain the records with respect to its interaction with clients.
In this regard, it is clarified that:

title: Review of regulatory requirement for maintenance of call records of institutional clients by Research Analysts or Research Entities
Review of regulatory requirement for maintenance of call records of institutional clients by Research Analysts or Research Entities
text:
(ii) Such records shall begin with first interaction with the client and shall continue till the completion of research services to the client.
(iii) RA or research entity are required to maintain these records for a period of five years. However, in case where dispute has been raised, such records shall be kept till resolution of the dispute or if SEBI desires that specific records be preserved, then such records shall be kept till further intimation from SEBI.”

title: Review of regulatory requirement for maintenance of call records of institutional clients by Research Analysts or Research Entities
text:
resolution of the dispute or if SEBI desires that specific records be preserved, then such records shall be kept till further intimation from SEBI.”
4.2. In Paragraph 33 of Annexure I (Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) related to regulatory provisions for Research Analysts) of Chapter VII of the Master Circular for RAs, the response to point iii. shall be replaced with the following: “iii. The requirement of maintenance of records of interactions with clients such as call recordings, emails, etc. is applicable for fee-paying as well as non-fee paying clients whereas non-fee paying clients are the clients receiving research services as a value added service along with other services availed from the research entity or any other entity at family/ group level on payable basis. For the purpose of abundant clarity, it is to be stated that call recording is not required if the interaction with client is made through means such as email, etc. for which digital footprint is available.

On October 27, 2025, amendments to the SEBI (Debenture Trustees) Regulations, 1993 (“DT Regulations”) were notified, inter alia, introducing Regulation 9C to provide clarity on the scope of permitted activities for debenture trustees. The provision, inter-alia, stipulates that a debenture trustee holding a valid certificate of registration may transfer its activities that are not regulated by SEBI to separate business unit(s) within a period of six months from the date of notification of the SEBI (Debenture Trustees) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025 in the Official Gazette, or within such extended period as may be specified by the Board.

The operational framework, including the terms and conditions governing activities undertaken by debenture trustees, was specified vide SEBI circular HO/17/11/12(3)2025-DDHS-POD1/ I/146/2025 dated November 25, 2025. Based on representations received from the industry highlighting operational challenges in establishing the necessary systems and processes for effective implementation, vide SEBI Circular dated April 28, 2026, DTs were granted an additional six months (i.e. up to October 27, 2026) for compliance with the aforesaid provisions.

Madam / Sir,

Subject: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs
1. Reference is drawn to the Depository Receipts Scheme, 2014 (‘DR Scheme’) notified by the Central Government vide notification number F.No. 9/1/2013-ECB dated October 21, 2014, as amended from time to time, which inter-alia states the following:

a. ‘depository receipt’ means a foreign currency denominated instrument, whether listed on an international exchange or not, issued by a foreign depository in a permissible jurisdiction on the back of permissible securities issued or transferred to that foreign depository and deposited with a domestic custodian and includes ‘global depository receipt’ as defined in section 2(44) of the Companies Act, 2013;

b. ‘permissible securities’ mean ‘securities’ as defined under section 2(h) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 and include similar instruments issued by private companies which:

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
which has not been specifically prohibited from accessing the capital market or dealing in securities.
2. Reference is also drawn to Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019 (‘NDI Rules’) notified by the Central Government vide notification S.O. 3732(E) dated October 17, 2019 which permits investment by persons resident outside India in depository receipts on units of InvITs.
3. Regulation 14(5C) of SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014 (‘InvIT Regulations’) provides that Depository Receipts may be issued on units of an InvIT subject to compliance with the InvIT Regulations and in such manner as may be specified by the Board. Accordingly, the framework for issuance of depository receipts on units of InvITs is specified hereunder.
4. Meaning of terms used
For the purpose of this framework –

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
4. Meaning of terms used
For the purpose of this framework –
(1) ‘Depository Receipt (‘DR’)’ means a foreign currency denominated instrument, listed on an international exchange, issued by a Foreign Depository in a Permissible Jurisdiction on the back of units of an InvIT issued or transferred to that foreign depository and deposited with a domestic custodian registered with the Board.
(2) ‘Foreign Depository’ means a person which:
a) is not prohibited from acquiring units of an InvIT;
b) is regulated in any of the Permissible Jurisdiction as defined in this framework; and
c) has legal capacity to issue DRs in the Permissible Jurisdiction.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
and
c) has legal capacity to issue DRs in the Permissible Jurisdiction.
(3) ‘Transfer of units of an InvIT by existing unitholders’ means deposit of existing units of the InvIT with a Domestic Custodian, for the purpose of issue of DRs, pursuant to formal agreement(s) among the Investment Manager on behalf of the InvIT and the Foreign Depository. For this purpose, the Investment Manager on behalf of the InvIT may enter into arrangement(s) with, Indian Depository, Domestic Custodian and existing unitholder(s), as may be necessary.
5. Eligibility Conditions

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
5. Eligibility Conditions
(1) InvIT shall be eligible to issue units or existing unitholders shall be eligible to transfer units, for the purpose of issue of DRs, if: a) the InvIT is in compliance with the requirements prescribed under the SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014 and any amendments thereof; b) the InvIT, parties to the InvIT and their directors, promoters and partners, and unitholders transferring units are not debarred from accessing the capital market by the Board; c) none of the parties to the InvIT and their directors, promoters, and partners is a promoter or director of any other Company or InvIT which is debarred from accessing the capital market by the Board; d) the InvIT, parties to the InvIT and their directors, promoters and partners, and unitholders transferring units are not wilful defaulter.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
d) the InvIT, parties to the InvIT and their directors, promoters and partners, and unitholders transferring units are not wilful defaulter.
e) the parties to the InvIT and their directors, promoters and partners, and unitholders transferring units are not fugitive economic offender.
(2) The conditions at paragraph 5(1)(b) to 5(1)(e) above shall not apply to the persons or entities, who were debarred in the past by the Board and the period of debarment is over as on the date of filing of the document as referred at paragraph 7(2).

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
were debarred in the past by the Board and the period of debarment is over as on the date of filing of the document as referred at paragraph 7(2).
(3) A DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), shall not be a person resident in India.

Explanation 1: For the purpose of this framework, ‘Beneficial Owner’ shall have the same meaning as provided in proviso to sub-rule 1 of rule 9 of Prevention of Money-Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005, as amended.

Explanation 2: The DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with this requirement.
6. Permissible Jurisdictions and International Exchanges

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
6. Permissible Jurisdictions and International Exchanges
(1) InvIT registered with the Board shall be permitted to issue units or facilitate transfer of units of existing unitholders, for the purpose of issue of DRs, only in Permissible Jurisdictions and the said DRs shall be listed on any of the specified International Exchange(s) of the Permissible Jurisdiction.

Explanation: For the purpose of this framework, ‘Permissible Jurisdictions’ and ‘International Exchange(s)’ shall be International Financial Services Centre in India - India International Exchange, NSE International Exchange.
(2) Listing of DRs on specified International Exchange shall meet the highest applicable level / standards for such listing by foreign issuers.
7. Issuance of Depository Receipts

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
7. Issuance of Depository Receipts
(1) The issuance of DRs on units of a privately placed InvIT shall be subject to the following conditions:
a) Each DR proposed to be issued on units of a Privately Placed InvIT shall be backed by at least that number of units which carry such value as specified under Regulation 14(2)(c) of the InvIT Regulations as on the date of filing of initial offer document with SEBI.

b) Any fresh issue of DR on units of a Privately Placed InvIT shall be subscribed only by such foreign investors as specified under Regulation 14(2)(b) of the InvIT Regulations.
Explanation: The Investment Manager of InvIT shall ensure that the agreement entered with the Foreign Depository, for the purpose of issue of DRs, provides that the DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), shall ensure compliance with the requirement mentioned at paragraph 7(1)(b) above.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
provides that the DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), shall ensure compliance with the requirement mentioned at paragraph 7(1)(b) above.
(2) The Investment Manager on behalf of InvIT shall, through merchant banker, file with the Board and the Recognized Stock Exchange(s), a copy of the initial offer document, by whatever name called, for any fresh issue of DRs. a) The Board shall endeavor to forward its comments, if any, in relation to compliance with the conditions stipulated in this framework or any other conditions as may be specified from time to time, to the Recognized Stock Exchange(s) within a period of 7 working days from the receipt of the document. b) Recognized Stock Exchange(s) shall take into consideration the comments of the Board while granting in-principle approval to InvIT and decide on the approval within 15 working days of receipt of application and required documents.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
while granting in-principle approval to InvIT and decide on the approval within 15 working days of receipt of application and required documents.
c) Further, final offer document, by whatever name called, for such issue shall be filed with Recognized Stock Exchange(s) and the Board for record purpose.
(3) InvIT proposing to do an initial offer of units and listing in India, and simultaneous issue of DRs and listing on International Exchange, shall seek in-principle and final approval from Recognized Stock Exchange in India as well as International Exchange. However, such issue or transfer of units for the purpose of issue of DRs shall be subsequent to the receipt of trading approval from the Recognized Stock Exchange for the initial offer of units.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
purpose of issue of DRs shall be subsequent to the receipt of trading approval from the Recognized Stock Exchange for the initial offer of units.
(4) Any fresh issue of DRs shall require prior approval of unit holders of the InvIT where vote cast in favor of the resolution shall be at least 75% of the total votes cast for the resolution.

Provided that the requirement to obtain unitholder approval shall not be applicable in case of issue of DR covered under sub-paragraph (3) above.

Provided further that a fresh unitholder approval shall not be required in case of subsequent offering of DRs in a permissible jurisdiction which is made within

the overall limit approved pursuant to a unitholders’ resolution in terms of this sub-paragraph.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
in a permissible jurisdiction which is made within

the overall limit approved pursuant to a unitholders’ resolution in terms of this sub-paragraph.
(5) For the purpose of any fresh issue and listing of DRs pursuant to ‘transfer by existing unitholders’, the InvIT shall provide an opportunity to all its existing unitholders to tender their units for participation in such listing of DRs.
(6) Fresh issue of DRs shall include first time offering as well as subsequent offering of DRs in a permissible jurisdiction, either by fresh issue of units of the InvIT or by way of transfer of units by existing unitholders. Further, any reissuance of DRs on account of two way fungibility shall not be considered fresh issue of DRs.
8. Obligations of the Investment Manager of InvIT

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
8. Obligations of the Investment Manager of InvIT
(1) The Investment Manager of InvIT shall ensure compliance with extant laws relating to issuance of DRs, including, requirements prescribed in this framework, the SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (‘FEMA’), Prevention of Money- Laundering Act, 2002, and rules and regulations made thereunder and any other applicable guidelines issued by Reserve Bank of India and Government.
For this purpose, the Investment Manager on behalf of InvIT, may also enter into necessary arrangements with Custodian, Indian Depository and Foreign Depository.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
the Investment Manager on behalf of InvIT, may also enter into necessary arrangements with Custodian, Indian Depository and Foreign Depository.
(2) The Investment Manager on behalf of the InvIT shall appoint a merchant banker in relation to issue of depository receipts. The merchant banker shall oversee all the compliances relating to issue of depository receipts and provide a compliance report which shall be placed at the meeting of the Board of Directors of the Investment Manager.
(3) The Investment Manager of InvIT shall ensure that DRs are issued only with units of the InvIT as the underlying.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
(3) The Investment Manager of InvIT shall ensure that DRs are issued only with units of the InvIT as the underlying.
(4) The Investment Manager shall ensure compliance with the minimum public unitholding requirement at the time of issuance of DRs.

Explanation: For the purpose of calculation of minimum public unitholding, the units held at the depository for the purpose of issue of DRs shall be treated as non-public unitholding.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
of minimum public unitholding, the units held at the depository for the purpose of issue of DRs shall be treated as non-public unitholding.
(5) The Investment Manager of InvIT shall ensure that the agreement entered with the Foreign Depository, for the purpose of issue of DRs, provides that the DR

holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), shall ensure compliance with the holding limits as per applicable SEBI Regulations including Regulation 14(2)(da) or Regulation 14(4)(ca) of the InvIT Regulations, as applicable, and Regulation 22(5C) of the InvIT Regulations. Explanation 1: For the purpose of ensuring compliance with Regulation 14(2)(da) or Regulation 14(4)(ca) of the InvIT Regulations, as applicable, units of InvIT held in the domestic market by the DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), shall be aggregated with units underlying the DR held by such persons. Explanation 2:

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
Explanation 2:
For the purpose of ensuring compliance with Regulation 22(5C) of the InvIT Regulations, units of InvIT held in the domestic market by the DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), along with persons acting in concert with them, shall be aggregated with units underlying the DR held by such persons.
9. Disclosures

The Investment Manager of InvIT shall ensure that any public disclosures made by the InvIT on International Exchange(s) in compliance with the requirements of the Permissible Jurisdiction, are also filed with the Recognized Stock Exchange within twenty four hours from such disclosure on International Exchange(s).

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
Jurisdiction, are also filed with the Recognized Stock Exchange within twenty four hours from such disclosure on International Exchange(s).
10. Voting rights

The Investment Manager of InvIT shall ensure that the agreement entered between the holder of DRs, the InvIT and the Depository provides that the voting rights on units underlying the DR, if any, shall be exercised by the DR holder through the Foreign Depository pursuant to voting instruction only from such DR holder.
11. Pricing

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
11. Pricing
(1) In case of a simultaneous listing of units on Recognized Stock Exchange(s) pursuant to an initial offer / preferential allotment / institutional placement under the SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, and DRs on the International Exchange, the price of issue or transfer of units, for the purpose of issue of DRs by Foreign Depository, shall not be less than the price for the initial offer / preferential allotment / institutional placement to domestic investors under the applicable laws.
(2) Where units are issued by an InvIT or transferred by the existing unitholders, for the purpose of issue of DRs by the Foreign Depository, the same shall be issued at a price, not less than the price applicable to a corresponding mode of issue of such units to domestic investors under the applicable laws.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of InvITs​
text:
at a price, not less than the price applicable to a corresponding mode of issue of such units to domestic investors under the applicable laws.
12. Obligations of Indian Depository, Foreign Depository and Domestic Custodian
(1) Domestic Custodian shall maintain records in respect of, and report to, Indian depositories all transactions in the nature of issue and cancellation of depository receipts.
(2) Indian Depositories shall coordinate among themselves and with Domestic Custodian to disseminate:
(a) number of units against which the DRs are outstanding; and,
(b) limit up to which units can be converted to DRs.

(3) For the purpose of sub-paragraph (2) above and mechanism for re-issuance of DRs, the provisions specified in paragraph 1 to paragraph 5 of Annexure 6 under Chapter 1 of the SEBI Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations dated December 30, 2024, as amended from time to time, shall be applicable. a. ‘depository receipt’ means a foreign currency denominated instrument, whether listed on an international exchange or not, issued by a foreign depository in a permissible jurisdiction on the back of permissible securities issued or transferred to that foreign depository and deposited with a domestic custodian and includes ‘global depository receipt’ as defined in section 2(44) of the Companies Act, 2013;

which has not been specifically prohibited from accessing the capital market or dealing in securities.

For the purpose of this framework –

4. Meaning of terms used

(2) ‘Foreign Depository’ means a person which:
a) is not prohibited from acquiring units of a REIT;
b) is regulated in any of the Permissible Jurisdiction as defined in this framework; and
c) has legal capacity to issue DRs in the Permissible Jurisdiction.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
and
c) has legal capacity to issue DRs in the Permissible Jurisdiction.
(3) ‘Transfer of units of a REIT by existing unitholders’ means deposit of existing units of the REIT with a Domestic Custodian, for the purpose of issue of DRs, pursuant to formal agreement(s) among the Manager on behalf of the REIT and the Foreign Depository. For this purpose, the Manager on behalf of the REIT may enter into arrangement(s) with, Indian Depository, Domestic Custodian and existing unitholder(s), as may be necessary.
5. Eligibility Conditions

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
5. Eligibility Conditions
(1) REIT shall be eligible to issue units or existing unitholders shall be eligible to transfer units, for the purpose of issue of DRs, if: a) the REIT is in compliance with the requirements prescribed under the SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014 and any amendments thereof; b) the REIT, parties to the REIT and their directors, promoters and partners, and unitholders transferring units are not debarred from accessing the capital market by the Board; c) none of the parties to the REIT and their directors, promoters, and partners is a promoter or director of any other Company or REIT which is debarred from accessing the capital market by the Board; d) the REIT, parties to the REIT and their directors, promoters and partners, and unitholders transferring units are not wilful defaulter.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
d) the REIT, parties to the REIT and their directors, promoters and partners, and unitholders transferring units are not wilful defaulter.
e) the parties to the REIT and their directors, promoters and partners, and unitholders transferring units are not fugitive economic offender.
(2) The conditions at paragraph 5(1)(b) to 5(1)(e) above shall not apply to the persons or entities, who were debarred in the past by the Board and the period of debarment is over as on the date of filing of the document as referred at paragraph 7(1).

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
were debarred in the past by the Board and the period of debarment is over as on the date of filing of the document as referred at paragraph 7(1).
(3) A DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), shall not be a person resident in India.

Explanation 1: For the purpose of this framework, ‘Beneficial Owner’ shall have the same meaning as provided in proviso to sub-rule 1 of rule 9 of Prevention of Money-Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005, as amended.

Explanation 2: The DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with this requirement.
6. Permissible Jurisdictions and International Exchanges

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
6. Permissible Jurisdictions and International Exchanges
(1) REIT registered with the Board shall be permitted to issue units or facilitate transfer of units of existing unitholders, for the purpose of issue of DRs, only in Permissible Jurisdictions and the said DRs shall be listed on any of the specified International Exchange(s) of the Permissible Jurisdiction.

Explanation: For the purpose of this framework, ‘Permissible Jurisdictions’ and ‘International Exchange(s)’ shall be International Financial Services Centre in India - India International Exchange, NSE International Exchange.
(2) Listing of DRs on specified International Exchange shall meet the highest applicable level / standards for such listing by foreign issuers.
7. Issuance of Depository Receipts

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
7. Issuance of Depository Receipts
(1) The Manager on behalf of REIT shall, through merchant banker, file with the Board and the Recognized Stock Exchange(s), a copy of the initial offer document, by whatever name called, for any fresh issue of DRs. a) The Board shall endeavor to forward its comments, if any, in relation to compliance with the conditions stipulated in this framework or any other

conditions as may be specified from time to time, to the Recognized Stock Exchange(s) within a period of 7 working days from the receipt of the document. b) Recognized Stock Exchange(s) shall take into consideration the comments of the Board while granting in-principle approval to REIT and decide on the approval within 15 working days of receipt of application and required documents.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
while granting in-principle approval to REIT and decide on the approval within 15 working days of receipt of application and required documents.
c) Further, final offer document, by whatever name called, for such issue shall be filed with Recognized Stock Exchange(s) and the Board for record purpose.
(2) REIT proposing to do an initial offer of units and listing in India, and simultaneous issue of DRs and listing on International Exchange, shall seek in-principle and final approval from Recognized Stock Exchange in India as well as International Exchange. However, such issue or transfer of units for the purpose of issue of DRs shall be subsequent to the receipt of trading approval from the Recognized Stock Exchange for the initial offer of units.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
purpose of issue of DRs shall be subsequent to the receipt of trading approval from the Recognized Stock Exchange for the initial offer of units.
(3) Any fresh issue of DRs shall require prior approval of unit holders of the REIT where vote cast in favor of the resolution shall be at least 75% of the total votes cast for the resolution.

Provided that the requirement to obtain unitholder approval shall not be applicable in case of issue of DR covered under sub-paragraph (2) above.

Provided further that a fresh unitholder approval shall not be required in case of subsequent offering of DRs in a permissible jurisdiction which is made within the overall limit approved pursuant to a unitholders’ resolution in terms of this sub-paragraph.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
in a permissible jurisdiction which is made within the overall limit approved pursuant to a unitholders’ resolution in terms of this sub-paragraph.
(4) For the purpose of any fresh issue and listing of DRs pursuant to ‘transfer by existing unitholders’, the REIT shall provide an opportunity to all its existing unitholders to tender their units for participation in such listing of DRs.
(5) Fresh issue of DRs shall include first time offering as well as subsequent offering of DRs in a permissible jurisdiction, either by fresh issue of units of the REIT or by way of transfer of units by existing unitholders. Further, any reissuance of DRs on account of two way fungibility shall not be considered fresh issue of DRs.
8. Obligations of the Manager of REIT

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
Further, any reissuance of DRs on account of two way fungibility shall not be considered fresh issue of DRs.
8. Obligations of the Manager of REIT
(1) The Manager of REIT shall ensure compliance with extant laws relating to issuance of DRs, including, requirements prescribed in this framework, the

SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (‘FEMA’), Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, and rules and regulations made thereunder and any other applicable guidelines issued by Reserve Bank of India and Government. For this purpose, the Manager on behalf of REIT, may also enter into necessary arrangements with Custodian, Indian Depository and Foreign Depository.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
this purpose, the Manager on behalf of REIT, may also enter into necessary arrangements with Custodian, Indian Depository and Foreign Depository.
(2) The Manager on behalf of the REIT shall appoint a merchant banker in relation to issue of depository receipts. The merchant banker shall oversee all the compliances relating to issue of depository receipts and provide a compliance report which shall be placed at the meeting of the Board of Directors of the Manager.
(3) The Manager of REIT shall ensure that DRs are issued only with units of the REIT as the underlying.
(4) The Manager shall ensure compliance with the minimum public unitholding requirement at the time of issuance of DRs.

Explanation: For the purpose of calculation of minimum public unitholding, the units held at the depository for the purpose of issue of DRs shall be treated as non-public unitholding.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
of minimum public unitholding, the units held at the depository for the purpose of issue of DRs shall be treated as non-public unitholding.
(5) The Manager of REIT shall ensure that the agreement entered with the Foreign Depository, for the purpose of issue of DRs, provides that the DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), shall ensure compliance with the holding limits as per applicable SEBI Regulations including Regulation 14(2)(bb) of the REIT Regulations and Regulation 22(6A) of the REIT Regulations. Explanation 1: For the purpose of ensuring compliance with Regulation 14(2)(bb) of the REIT Regulations, units of REIT held in the domestic market by the DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), shall be aggregated with units underlying the DR held by such persons. Explanation 2:

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
Explanation 2:
For the purpose of ensuring compliance with Regulation 22(6A) of the REIT Regulations, units of REIT held in the domestic market by the DR holder, including its Beneficial Owner(s), along with persons acting in concert with them, shall be aggregated with units underlying the DR held by such persons.
9. Disclosures

The Manager of REIT shall ensure that any public disclosures made by the REIT on International Exchange(s) in compliance with the requirements of the Permissible Jurisdiction, are also filed with the Recognized Stock Exchange within twenty four hours from such disclosure on International Exchange(s).

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
Jurisdiction, are also filed with the Recognized Stock Exchange within twenty four hours from such disclosure on International Exchange(s).
10. Voting rights
The Manager of REIT shall ensure that the agreement entered between the holder of DRs, the REIT and the Depository provides that the voting rights on units underlying the DR, if any, shall be exercised by the DR holder through the Foreign Depository pursuant to voting instruction only from such DR holder.
11. Pricing

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
11. Pricing
(1) In case of a simultaneous listing of units on Recognized Stock Exchange(s) pursuant to an initial offer / preferential allotment / institutional placement under the SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, and DRs on the International Exchange, the price of issue or transfer of units, for the purpose of issue of DRs by Foreign Depository, shall not be less than the price for the initial offer / preferential allotment / institutional placement to domestic investors under the applicable laws.
(2) Where units are issued by a REIT or transferred by the existing unitholders, for the purpose of issue of DRs by the Foreign Depository, the same shall be issued at a price, not less than the price applicable to a corresponding mode of issue of such units to domestic investors under the applicable laws.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
at a price, not less than the price applicable to a corresponding mode of issue of such units to domestic investors under the applicable laws.
12. Obligations of Indian Depository, Foreign Depository and Domestic Custodian
(1) Domestic Custodian shall maintain records in respect of, and report to, Indian depositories all transactions in the nature of issue and cancellation of depository receipts.
(2) Indian Depositories shall coordinate among themselves and with Domestic Custodian to disseminate:
(a) number of units against which the DRs are outstanding; and,
(b) limit up to which units can be converted to DRs.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
(a) number of units against which the DRs are outstanding; and,
(b) limit up to which units can be converted to DRs.
(3) For the purpose of sub-paragraph (2) above and mechanism for re-issuance of DRs, the provisions specified in paragraph 1 to paragraph 5 of Annexure 6 under Chapter 1 of the SEBI Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations dated December 30, 2024, as amended from time to time, shall be applicable. The reference to the following terms made therein, should be construed as follows, for the purpose of this requirement, unless otherwise required:

text:

(4) The Foreign Depository shall not issue the DRs unless the Domestic Custodian has confirmed the receipt of units underlying the DRs.
13. Words and expressions used and not defined in this framework but defined in the Depository Receipts Scheme, 2014, the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, the Depositories Act, 1996, the Companies Act, 2013, the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 or the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, and rules and regulations made thereunder shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them, as the case may be, in those Acts, unless the context requires otherwise.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
made thereunder shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them, as the case may be, in those Acts, unless the context requires otherwise.
14. Power to remove difficulties

In case of any difficulties in the application or interpretation or to relax strict enforcement of the requirements of the framework for issue of DRs, the Board may issue clarifications through guidance notes or circulars after receipt of request from the issuer.
15. Applicability

The provisions of this Circular shall come into force with immediate effect.

title: Framework for Issuance of Depository Receipts on Units of REITs​
text:
15. Applicability

The provisions of this Circular shall come into force with immediate effect.
16. This circular is issued in exercise of powers conferred under Section 11(1) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 read with the provisions of Regulations 14(12A) and Regulation 33 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014, to protect the interests of investors in securities market and to promote the development of, and to regulate the securities market. This circular is issued with the approval of the competent authority.
17. The recognized Stock Exchanges and Indian REITs Association are advised to disseminate the contents of this Circular on their website.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
CIRCULAR

HO/38/30/12(3)2026-MIRSD-POD2/I/25175/2026 November 04, 2026

To,

All intermediaries registered with SEBI under Section 12 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992;
Recognised Stock Exchanges;
Recognised Clearing Corporations; and
All Depositories

Dear Sir/ Madam,

Subject: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
1. SEBI vide Master Circular SEBI/HO/MIRSD/SECFATF/P/CIR/2023/169 dated October 12, 2023 (‘KYC Master Circular’), inter-alia, specifies the Know Your Client (KYC) requirements for on-boarding client by an intermediary and a framework for validation of KYC records by a KYC Registration Agency (KRA)1.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
(KYC) requirements for on-boarding client by an intermediary and a framework for validation of KYC records by a KYC Registration Agency (KRA)1.
2. The extant provisions of the KYC Master Circular, inter-alia, requires an intermediary to ensure that, during digital KYC, the physical location of the client is in India. This requirement in effect restricts a client outside India, at the time of on- boarding, to submit the KYC documents and complete the KYC process digitally.
3. In order to ease the process of on-boarding of an individual Person Resident Outside India (PROI)2 client, it has been decided to review the existing provisions governing the KYC process. Individual PROI client shall mean Non-Resident Indian (NRI)3, Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)4 or foreign national.
1 KYC Registration Agencies as per SEBI (Know Your Client Registration Agencies) Regulations, 2011;

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
Force (FATF) compliant country5 and the intermediary may accept digital submission of KYC information and supporting documents from such client.
4.2. KRA shall tag individual attributes in the KYC record as “validated”, if verified with official or source database. All KYC records shall be portable i.e. can be shared with another intermediary, irrespective of every individual attribute being validated or not.
4.3. The intermediary may rely on the KYC undertaken by a SEBI registered intermediary or by an entity regulated by other financial sector regulators, based on record obtained from KRA or Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCRR).
4.4. The authorised official of the intermediary shall be present during Video In Person Verification of a client and the VIPV process shall be subject to concurrent audit.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
of the intermediary shall be present during Video In Person Verification of a client and the VIPV process shall be subject to concurrent audit.
5. Accordingly, the on-boarding of individual PROI clients through intermediaries and KRAs, are being detailed below:
5.1. The intermediary shall, at the time of commencement of an account based relationship, identify its client, verify the identity and obtain information on the purpose and intended nature of the business relationship.
5.2. When the client approaches an intermediary to initiate an account based relationship or update KYC, the intermediary shall seek the PAN and CKYC ID6 from the client, if available. Thereafter, the intermediary shall retrieve the KYC records (i.e. information and documents) from KRA and CKYCRR.
5.3. If the client record already exists, the intermediary shall obtain additional details from the client only when:

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
or
5.3.5. to perform enhanced due diligence (EDD) or to build an appropriate risk profile of the client.
5.4. The intermediary shall provide the updated KYC information of the client to KRA, which shall update the existing KYC record and inform all intermediaries that avail of the services of the KRA in respect of that client, in line with the provisions of the SEBI {KYC (Know Your Client) Registration Agencies) Regulations, 2011 (‘KRA Regulations’).
5.5. The KYC process shall involve the following aspects:

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
5.5. The KYC process shall involve the following aspects:
5.5.1. PAN:

a. The intermediary shall collect the PAN of the client and verify the same with the Income Tax Database, without insisting on producing the original PAN or providing a copy thereof.

b. The KRA shall also verify the PAN and the name of the client, as mentioned in the KYC form, with the Income Tax Database.
Accordingly, the said attribute shall be tagged as “validated” in the KYC record.
5.5.2. Passport:

a. The intermediary shall collect a copy of the Passport from the client.

b. The intermediary shall also collect Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card from the client, as applicable.

c. The intermediary shall verify the passport of the client, if feasible.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
c. The intermediary shall verify the passport of the client, if feasible.
7 OVD and deemed to be OVD, as defined under the Prevention of Money Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 (PMLR);

d. KRA shall verify the passport of the client, if feasible. Accordingly, the said attribute shall be tagged as “validated” in the KYC record.
5.5.3. KYC form:

a. The intermediary shall collect the KYC information from the client, as per CKYCRR template8 prescribed for “individuals”, in physical or through app, website or digital mode.

b. The intermediary can collect the filled KYC form in any of the following manners:

i. original physical form; or

ii. scanned copy of physical form, under electronic signature9; or

iii. digital KYC form, under electronic signature.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
original physical form; or

ii. scanned copy of physical form, under electronic signature9; or

iii. digital KYC form, under electronic signature.
5.5.4. Specimen signature:

a. The intermediary shall collect specimen signature from the client in any of the following forms:

i. wet signature on the physical KYC form; or

ii. cropped image of specimen signature, under electronic signature.

b. In case of digital submission of specimen signature, the client shall do wet signature before the intermediary during Video In Person Verification (VIPV), and the intermediary in turn shall verify if the said signature matches with the client’s submission.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
during Video In Person Verification (VIPV), and the intermediary in turn shall verify if the said signature matches with the client’s submission.
5.5.5. Proof of Identity and Proof of Address:

a. The intermediary shall collect any one of the specified officially valid documents or deemed officially valid documents, for proof of identity and proof of address, from the client. For this purpose, the current address for an individual PROI client shall be an overseas address.
8 KYC template provided by Central Registry of Securitization Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India (CERSAI);

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
8 KYC template provided by Central Registry of Securitization Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India (CERSAI);
9 “electronic signature” shall have the meaning as defined under the Information Technology Act, 2000; b. In case the officially valid documents presented by a foreign national does not contain the details of address, a document issued by a Government department of a foreign jurisdiction and letter issued by a Foreign Embassy or Mission in India can be collected by the intermediary as proof of address. c. The intermediary shall verify the address mentioned in the KYC form with the address mentioned in the officially valid document or deemed officially valid document submitted by the client and with the official or source database, if feasible. d. The KRA shall also verify the address mentioned in the KYC form with the address mentioned in the officially valid document or deemed officially valid document submitted by the client and with the official or source database, if feasible.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
in the officially valid document or deemed officially valid document submitted by the client and with the official or source database, if feasible.
Accordingly, the said attributes shall be tagged as “validated” in the KYC record.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
Accordingly, the said attributes shall be tagged as “validated” in the KYC record.
5.5.6. Original, Seen and Verified (OSV): a. The intermediary shall see and verify the original of the officially valid document or deemed officially valid document submitted by the client, for proof of identity and proof of address, and collect the physical self-attested copies of the same. b. In case the original of the officially valid document or deemed officially valid document is not produced for verification, then the intermediary shall collect any of the following: i. equivalent e-document of officially valid document or deemed officially valid document through Digi Locker; or

ii. equivalent e-document of officially valid document or deemed officially valid document, issued by the issuing authority through any verifiable mechanism; or

iii. One Time Password (OTP) or biometric or face authentication based Aadhaar e-KYC authentication; or

iv.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
or

iii. One Time Password (OTP) or biometric or face authentication based Aadhaar e-KYC authentication; or

iv.
copy of officially valid document attested by any of the certifying authorities (i.e. Notary Public, authorised official of overseas branch of Scheduled Commercial Banks registered in India, branches of overseas banks with whom Indian banks have

relationships, Court Magistrate, Judge, Indian Embassy or Consulate General of the country where the client resides). c. The intermediary shall ensure that the details of the authorised official undertaking the OSV and the date and time stamp are recorded at the time of OSV. d. The intermediary shall ensure that the copy of the certified OVD provided by the client contains the date, location, name and license number/ employee code, if any, of the certifying authority.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
the certified OVD provided by the client contains the date, location, name and license number/ employee code, if any, of the certifying authority.
5.5.7. Mobile number and email id:

a. The intermediary shall collect the mobile number (Indian or international) and the email id of the client. The mobile number and email id recorded in Aadhaar may be preferred.

b. The intermediary shall verify the mobile number, if feasible, and the email id of the client through OTP or any other verifiable mechanism.

c. If the mobile number of the client cannot be verified, then the intermediary shall ensure that all communications are sent on the verified email id of such client.

d. The KRA shall also verify the mobile number, if feasible, and the email id of the client through OTP or any other verifiable mechanism.
Accordingly, the said attributes shall be tagged as “validated” in the KYC record.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
Accordingly, the said attributes shall be tagged as “validated” in the KYC record.
5.5.8. In-Person Verification (IPV): a. The intermediary shall carry out IPV of the client and ensure that the details of the authorised official undertaking the IPV and the date and time stamp are recorded at the time of IPV. b. In case the physical IPV is not feasible, the intermediary shall undertake VIPV of the client, while ensuring the following: i. the client consent is recorded in an auditable and alteration proof manner; ii. the VIPV infrastructure has features of random action initiation for client response to establish that the interactions are not pre- recorded; iii. the uninterrupted video recording contains the live GPS co- ordinates (geo-tagging) of the client and the date and time stamp through use of tamper proof technology; iv. the VIPV infrastructure prevents connection from spoofed IP addresses, using VPNs or proxy servers; v.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
iv. the VIPV infrastructure prevents connection from spoofed IP addresses, using VPNs or proxy servers; v.
the IP address of the client, as captured, emanates from India or from any of the FATF compliant country and matches with the country specified by the client in the KYC form and officially valid document or deemed officially valid document; vi. the photo of the client is clearly captured in the VIPV process and matches with the photo submitted by the client in the form and officially valid document or deemed officially valid document; vii. there is end to end encryption of data between customer device and the hosting point of application/ digital platform at the intermediary; viii. the authorised official of the intermediary is present during the VIPV process; ix. the VIPV infrastructure uses components which verify face liveness and detect spoofs, if any; such liveliness check does not result in exclusion of person with special needs; and

x.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
such liveliness check does not result in exclusion of person with special needs; and

x.
the VIPV process is subject to concurrent audit, to ensure the integrity of process and its acceptability of the outcome. c. The intermediary may incorporate additional safety and security features in the VIPV process, as per its risk management policy.
5.6. Reliance of third party KYC:
5.6.1. The intermediary may rely on the KYC undertaken by another SEBI registered intermediary, as per record obtained from the KRA. The KYC record shared by KRA with intermediary shall have each attribute wise tagging for whether it is “validated” or not.
5.6.2. The intermediary may also rely on the KYC undertaken by an entity regulated by any of the other Financial Sector Regulators10, as per record obtained from the CKYCRR.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
also rely on the KYC undertaken by an entity regulated by any of the other Financial Sector Regulators10, as per record obtained from the CKYCRR.
5.6.3. The intermediary shall have the ultimate responsibility for the KYC of its clients, including undertaking enhanced due diligence appropriate to the risk profile of the clients.
5.7. Upon completion of the KYC of individual PROI client, the intermediary shall provide the KYC information to KRA within 3 working days from the date of completion of KYC process.
5.8. The intermediary shall ensure that the infrastructure being used for the KYC process is in compliance with the Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience Framework issued by SEBI.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
that the infrastructure being used for the KYC process is in compliance with the Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience Framework issued by SEBI.
5.9. All documents submitted by an individual PROI client to the intermediary should be in English. In case the document is in any other language, then the client shall get the document translated to English and attested by a certifying authority, before submission to the intermediary.
5.10. The aforementioned process shall also be applicable for re-KYC of the client in a FATF compliant country.
6. In cases where an individual foreign national seeks registration as a Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI), the provisions of Master Circular for Foreign Portfolio Investors, Designated Depository Participants and Eligible Foreign Investors ref.
no. SEBI/HO/AFD/AFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/70 dated May 30, 2024 or amendments thereof, shall be applicable.

title: Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
Review of Know Your Client process for individual Person Resident Outside India clients
text:
KYC undertaken by intermediaries prior to the date of this circular coming into effect, shall continue to be governed by the extant KYC provisions.
9. This circular is being issued in exercise of powers conferred under Section 11(1) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, to protect the interests of investors in securities and to promote the development of, and to regulate the securities market.
10. This circular is available on the SEBI website at www.sebi.gov.in, under the category, ‘Legal → Circulars’.
