CIRCULAR

HO/24/13/(1)2026-IMD-POD-2/I/25242/2026 November 05, 2026 All Mutual Funds All Asset Management Companies (AMCs) All Trustees / Trustee Companies All Registered Custodians All Recognised Clearing Corporations All Recognised Stock Exchanges All Registered Stock Brokers through Recognised Stock Exchanges Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI)

Dear Sir / Madam,
Subject: Framework for net settlement of funds for transactions undertaken by mutual fund schemes in cash market

title: Framework for net settlement of funds for transactions undertaken by mutual fund schemes in cash market
text:
Framework for net settlement of funds for transactions undertaken by mutual fund schemes in cash market
1. SEBI Master Circular for Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations dated December 30, 2024, inter-alia, stipulates that no institutional investor shall be allowed to do day trading, i.e., square off their transactions intra-day. Accordingly, transactions undertaken by institutional investors in the cash market are required to be delivery- backed and settled on gross basis at the custodian or client level.
2. SEBI, vide Circular dated April 24, 2026, permitted net settlement of funds for outright transactions undertaken by Foreign Portfolio Investors in the cash market while retaining gross settlement of securities, to be implemented by December 31, 2026.

title: Framework for net settlement of funds for transactions undertaken by mutual fund schemes in cash market
text:
undertaken by Foreign Portfolio Investors in the cash market while retaining gross settlement of securities, to be implemented by December 31, 2026.
3. With a view to enhance operational efficiency, reduce temporary funding requirements and improving settlement efficiency for mutual fund schemes, it has been decided to permit net settlement of funds, at the level of an individual mutual fund scheme, for outright transactions undertaken in the cash segment of stock exchanges, subject to the conditions specified in this circular. Settlement of securities shall continue to be on gross basis.
4. For the purpose of this circular, “outright transaction” shall mean either a purchase transaction or a sale transaction, but not both, in a security in the same settlement cycle undertaken by a mutual fund scheme.

title: Framework for net settlement of funds for transactions undertaken by mutual fund schemes in cash market
text:
either a purchase transaction or a sale transaction, but not both, in a security in the same settlement cycle undertaken by a mutual fund scheme.
5. Accordingly, where a mutual fund scheme has both purchase and sale transactions in the same security within the same settlement cycle, such transactions in that security shall be treated as non-outright transactions for that settlement cycle and shall not be eligible for net settlement of funds under this circular.

Page | 2
6. The net settlement framework shall not apply to transactions such as derivative transactions, securities lending and borrowing transactions, short sale-related transactions and any other transaction not expressly covered under this circular.
Framework for net settlement of funds
7. Scheme-level netting:

title: Framework for net settlement of funds for transactions undertaken by mutual fund schemes in cash market
text:
Framework for net settlement of funds
7. Scheme-level netting:
7.1. Netting of funds shall be permitted only within the same mutual fund scheme and within the same settlement cycle.
7.2. No netting shall be permitted across different schemes of the same mutual fund.
7.3. No adjustment of obligations shall be permitted between two or more schemes or portfolios.
7.4. The AMC and custodian shall ensure that the netting mechanism does not affect scheme-wise accounting, NAV computation, asset allocation, investment limits or unit-holder interest.
8. Treatment of residual obligations:
8.1. In case the value of outright sale transactions is less than the value of outright purchase transactions, the residual fund obligation shall be funded by the concerned mutual fund scheme.

title: Framework for net settlement of funds for transactions undertaken by mutual fund schemes in cash market
text:
is less than the value of outright purchase transactions, the residual fund obligation shall be funded by the concerned mutual fund scheme.
8.2. In case the value of outright sale transactions exceeds the value of outright purchase transactions, such excess outright sale proceeds shall not be adjusted against non-outright purchase obligations.
8.3. Non-outright purchase obligations shall continue to be funded separately on gross basis.
8.4. An illustration of obligations of mutual fund scheme under current practice and under net settlement framework is placed at Annexure.
9. Securities settlement, STT and stamp duty
9.1. Settlement of securities shall continue to be carried out on gross basis between the mutual fund scheme and the custodian.
9.2. Securities Transaction Tax and stamp duty shall continue to be charged on delivery basis, as applicable.

title: Framework for net settlement of funds for transactions undertaken by mutual fund schemes in cash market
text:
9.2. Securities Transaction Tax and stamp duty shall continue to be charged on delivery basis, as applicable.
9.3. The proposed netting shall not alter the delivery-backed nature of institutional trades in the cash market.
10. Operational safeguards
10.1. AMCs and custodians shall ensure that adequate systems and controls are put in place for scheme-wise identification of outright purchase and sale transactions, non-outright transactions, gross fund obligations, net fund obligations and securities pay-in and pay-out obligations.

Page | 3
10.2. The custodian shall maintain a clear audit trail of gross obligations, netted fund obligations and excluded non-outright transactions.
10.3. The AMC and custodian shall ensure that no cross-scheme adjustment or inter- scheme funding takes place under this framework.

12.3. Clearing Corporations shall continue to settle obligations at the clearing member/custodian level in accordance with the extant settlement framework.
13. System readiness
13.1. AMCs, custodians, stock brokers, recognised Stock Exchanges and recognised Clearing Corporations are advised to make necessary changes in their systems and processes to give effect to the provisions of this circular.
13.2. AMCs and custodians shall jointly confirm system readiness before implementation.

title: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
text:
CIRCULAR
HO/19/34/11(6)2026-AFD-POD1/I/25244/2026 November 05, 2026
To,
All Alternative Investment Funds (“AIFs”)
All recognised Accreditation Agencies
All Portfolio Managers
All Investment Advisers
All Research Analysts
All Mutual Funds

Sir/ Madam,
Sub: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
1. With an objective to ease and expedite the process of accreditation, the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012 (“AIF Regulations”), have been amended and notified on October 15, 2026.
2. The modalities for implementing these provisions are specified below.
3. Manager led accreditation

title: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
text:
2. The modalities for implementing these provisions are specified below.
3. Manager led accreditation
3.1. A Manager may determine and record an investor’s accredited status at onboarding or during the tenure of a scheme, after verifying that the investor meets eligibility criteria under the AIF Regulations and this circular. For the purpose of accreditation, “Manager” means the manager of an AIF, the asset management company of a Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) (as defined under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026) or a portfolio manager (as defined under SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026), as applicable.

title: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
text:
under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026) or a portfolio manager (as defined under SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026), as applicable.
3.2. A determination made by a Manager shall be recognised across Managers of the same Group for AIFs, SIFs and portfolio management services during the validity period specified in paragraph 4. “Group” has the meaning assigned to “corporate group” under Explanation I to Regulation 19F(1) of the AIF Regulations.
3.3. An Investment Adviser (IA) or Research Analyst (RA) shall not determine accredited status of an investor independently, but may rely on a valid determination made by a Manager in its Group.
3.4. The Manager shall record the accreditation status of an investor and shall confirm the same in writing to the investor. The Manager shall inform the investor of the date of accreditation and the validity period.

title: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
text:
The Manager shall inform the investor of the date of accreditation and the validity period.
3.5. Manager led accreditation is an additional and optional route. The Accreditation Agency route shall continue to be available. When an investor furnishes a valid certificate of accreditation from a recognised Accreditation Agency, the Manager shall rely on it and shall not conduct fresh determination during its validity.
4. Validity of accreditation
4.1. Accreditation determined by a Manager shall be valid for a period of three years from the date of accreditation.
4.2. Accreditation shall be determined afresh each time an investor is onboarded by a Manager who is not of the same Group.
4.3. A certificate of accreditation issued by a recognised Accreditation Agency shall be valid for three years from the date of accreditation.

title: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
text:
4.3. A certificate of accreditation issued by a recognised Accreditation Agency shall be valid for three years from the date of accreditation.
4.4. An investor who is an Accredited Investor at the time of onboarding into a scheme shall continue to be reckoned as an Accredited Investor for the remaining life of that scheme.
4.5. A certificate of accreditation issued before the date of applicability of this circular shall remain valid for its unexpired period of validity.
5. Securities market exposure
5.1. The minimum qualifying securities market exposure shall be INR 5 crore in the case of an individual, Hindu Undivided Family, family trust or sole proprietorship, and INR 20 crore in the case of a body corporate or a trust other than a family trust.
5.2. The following shall qualify as securities market exposure:
5.2.1. Securities held in dematerialised form;

title: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
text:
The certificate shall identify the nature of securities, valuation date, and value.
6. Safeguards for Manager led accreditation
6.1. Accountability: A Manager undertaking accreditation shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with the prescribed eligibility criteria and with the requirements of this circular.
6.2. Maintenance of records: A Manager shall maintain all records, supporting documents and verification evidence relied upon for the determining accredited status, for atleast five years from the date of accreditation or until five years after the investor ceases to be an investor in any scheme managed by the Manager, whichever is later. The records shall be made available for inspection as and when sought.
6.3. Audit: Periodic internal audit and compliance review of the accreditation process shall be carried out as part of any existing audit undertaken by the Manager.

title: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
text:
internal audit and compliance review of the accreditation process shall be carried out as part of any existing audit undertaken by the Manager.
6.4. Accreditation policy: Every Manager undertaking accreditation shall adopt an accreditation policy specifying:
6.4.1. conflict of interest controls, including separation of the accreditation function from the business development and distribution function;
6.4.2. an escalation and grievance redressal process for resolving investor concerns arising from the determination of accredited status; and
6.4.3. record retention infrastructure, covering inter alia data privacy and cybersecurity, so that the confidentiality of the information submitted by investors is protected.

7. Eligibility criteria and documents for verification

7. Eligibility criteria and documents for verification
7.1. The Manager or Accreditation Agency, as applicable, shall verify that the applicant meets the eligibility criteria specified under Regulation 2(1)(ab) of the AIF Regulations, based on income, net worth or securities market exposure, using the documents specified in the table below:

8. Accreditation of Limited Liability Partnerships
8.1. A Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) set up under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, shall be recognised as an Accredited Investor where each partner independently satisfies the eligibility criteria for accreditation, applicable to that partner as on the date of determination.
8.2. Where a partner is itself a body corporate, including another LLP, a firm or a trust, that partner shall independently satisfy the eligibility criteria applicable to it.
9. Persons Resident Outside India

title: Review of the framework for Accredited Investors
text:
9. Persons Resident Outside India
9.1. A Person Resident Outside India, as defined under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, shall be deemed to be an Accredited Investor and shall not be required to obtain a certificate of accreditation or undergo Manager led accreditation.
9.2. The Manager shall record the basis on which the investor has been identified as a Person Resident Outside India.
9.3. Deemed Accredited Investor status shall not dilute the obligations of an AIF and its Manager, as reporting entities under the Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002 and the rules framed thereunder, to conduct client due diligence, identify beneficial owners and comply with applicable requirements relating to source of funds.
10. Applicability
10.1. This circular shall come into force with immediate effect.
